title: Estimating College Costs and Making a Savings Plan
seo_title: Grade 8 Paying for College Worksheets: Costs and Savings Plans (TEKS 8.12G, STAAR)
standard_text: 8.12G estimate the cost of a two-year and four-year college education, including family contribution, and devise a periodic savings plan for accumulating the money needed to contribute to the total cost of attendance for at least the first year of college
meta_desc: Free Grade 8 personal financial literacy worksheets for Texas TEKS 8.12G: estimate college costs, two-year and four-year totals, family contribution and a savings plan. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Savings per month = amount needed ÷ months left.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • The cost of attendance includes tuition and fees, housing and food, books, transportation and other costs.
  • A two-year degree is about 2 years of cost; a four-year degree is about 4 years.
  • Grants, scholarships and work reduce what the family contributes.
  • A savings plan divides the amount needed by the number of months or years until college.

Examples

Example

$9,600 needed in 4 years

4 × 12 = 48 months

9,600 ÷ 48

Answer: $200 a month

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Counting only tuitionAdd housing, food, books and other costs.
Using one year for a four-year totalMultiply by the number of years.
Dividing by years when months are asked4 years is 48 months.

faq.a: Estimate the cost of a two-year and four-year college education, including family contribution, and devise a periodic savings plan for accumulating the money needed to contribute to the total cost of attendance for at least the first year of college.
The part of the cost the family pays after grants, scholarships and work.

faq.q: Does interest help a savings plan?
faq.a: Yes. Interest means the family needs to deposit a little less.
It usually costs less for the first two years.
